title: CatalogDocument
description:
The schema-emission root: one object that references the three wire
shapes, so a single `schema_for!` call produces one self-contained
document with every `$defs` entry the TS emitter needs (§5.1(a) —
"the single machine description of the catalog").

AudioDevice.description:
One audio output device (§2.6 `audio.list-devices`). On web there is
exactly one pseudo-device (`webaudio`).

isDefault.description: Whether this is the current default output.

codecParams.description: Opaque codec parameters, when the container carries them.

id.description:
Stable bookmark id — creation-ordered from 1, unique within the
session (never reused after a delete; matches the keymap's
1-based bookmark slots, keymaps/default.toml `set-bookmark-N`).

CodecDescriptor.description:
Clean-room codec descriptor (§2.2: `{ fourcc, description, profile,
level }`). All fields optional — containers differ wildly in what
they report. `[VERIFY]` — field granularity to be audited against
Phase-0 format inventory.

fourcc.description: FourCC when the container carries one.

CommandError.description:
The command error (doc 05 §1.6): stage + code + redaction-safe
message + machine-readable details.

# Redaction (V8, MP §12)

`message` is **display-safe by construction**: [`CommandError::new`]
routes every message through [`redact`], which masks userinfo in
URLs (`user:pass@` → `***@`) and collapses absolute paths to their
final component (`/home/alice/x.mkv` → `…/x.mkv`). Raw diagnostic
chains belong to the log sink only — they never enter this type.
`details` values pass through the same redactor.

CommandListing.description:
One row of `system.list-commands` (§2.12, `[PROPOSAL]` per doc 05):
lets UIs and the control server build menus and validate keymaps
without hardcoding the catalog.

requires.description: Other command ids this one requires to be usable (empty in v1).

since.description:
Catalog version the command appeared in (`"1"` for the v1
namespace, §6.1).

CommandOutcome.description:
The truthful-UI outcome split (doc 05 §1.4 — hard contract):
`Accepted` is "validated and queued/started", `Completed` is "the
engine confirms it happened (in this response)".

oneOf.description:
Class A: queued/started. `generation` is the generation under which the
completion event will arrive — the NEW generation for generation-bumping
commands, the current generation otherwise (§4.2).

Class S: the engine confirms completion in this response; no
event is required (rule C2).

CommandRequest.description:
One host → engine request (doc 05 §1.6). Generic over the command
payload `C` — card 1.D4 instantiates `CommandRequest<Command>` with
the catalog enum; the envelope semantics here are payload-blind.

oneOf.description: `session.open` — open a source as a new session (class A).

`session.close` — close the session (class S, gen-bumping,
idempotent).

`playback.stop` — tear down the pipeline; the session survives
(class A, gen-bumping).
`playback.step-frame` — auto-pause then step one frame (A, gen).

`playback.set-position` — seek by fraction (class A, gen-bumping;
slider/scrubber ergonomics, §2.4).

`tracks.set-subtitle-track` — selection over parsed streams
(class S — no pipeline invalidation).
`audio.set-volume` — the response says what IS (class S).

`video.set-fullscreen` — **target: shell** (class S; the only
shell-routed command in v1, §1.1.3).

path.description:
Explicit output path; `None` uses `video.screenshot-dir` +
the filename template (config). `[PROPOSAL]` web path policy
(§2.7 — the binding converts to a browser download).

oneOf.description:
`subtitle.add-file` — external subtitle file (class A).
`[VERIFY]` — `PathSpec` (§2.8) is a plain path string here; the
web host's transferred-`Blob` variant needs the binding-layer
param extension before apps/web consumes it.

select.description: Whether to select the track once parsed (default true).

oneOf.description:
`subtitle.set-sync` — relative shift; the result carries the new
absolute delay (class S).
`playlist.enqueue` — model edit, does not open (class S).
`playlist.play-item` — full open lifecycle on that item (A).
`playlist.next` — open lifecycle of the next item (class A).
`playlist.skip` — open lifecycle of item at `current + n` (A).

`playlist.remove` — removing the playing item starts the advance
lifecycle (class S for the model edit).
`playlist.clear` — stops playback if an item was playing (S).

path.description: Output file (format defaults from the extension).

oneOf.description:
`media.get-bookmarks` — the session's bookmark list (class S,
issue #32).

`media.add-bookmark` — bookmark a position (class S, issue #32;
no pipeline invalidation — not gen-bumping).
`system.plugin-disable` — takes effect next session if in use (S).

CommandResponse.description:
One engine → host response (doc 05 §1.6). `request_id` is echoed,
always; `session`/`generation` are the context at handling time.

CommandResult.description:
The completed payload of a class-S command (doc 05 §2 tables'
*Result* column; class-A commands never produce one — §1.4 C2/C3).

Internally tagged (`"kind"`) so the wire form is
`{ "completed": { "kind": "audio-volume", "volume": 0.8 } }` inside
[`CommandOutcome::Completed`](crate::envelope::CommandOutcome).
Variants are shared by shape across commands (see the module docs).

oneOf.description: Nothing to report (`session.close`, playlist model edits).

tracks.description: Every track of the current media.

oneOf.description:
`audio.set-volume`/`get-volume` — the applied volume (the truth,
after device clipping).

`audio.set-delay`, `video.set-delay`, `subtitle.set-sync` — an
applied delay in ms (for `set-sync`, the new absolute total).

`media.get-bookmarks` / `media.remove-bookmark` — the bookmark
list (issue #32; remove answers with the updated list).

`config.get-setting` — value + schema metadata.
`[VERIFY]` — `schema_meta` is a free-form string map until the
settings-schema crate defines its wire projection.

restartRequired.description: Whether a restart is required for full effect.

applied.description: Whether the plugin is now enabled.

takesEffect.description: When the toggle takes effect (per manifest).

oneOf.description:
Synchronous-complete: pure queries; atomic mutations with bounded
work, no pipeline invalidation, no unbounded I/O. The response
IS the completion evidence (C2).

Async-observed: reconfigures the pipeline, performs unbounded
I/O, or its effect is only observable through engine state.
Answers `Accepted`; completes via a named event (C3).

anyRestartRequired.description: Whether any setting in the area requires a restart.

nameKey.description: Localization key for the area's display name.

settingCount.description: Number of settings in the area.

oneOf.description: Crop to a rectangle (pixel offsets from the top-left).

DecoderInfo.description:
One decoder of the engine's registry (§2.12 `system.get-engine-info`
— hardware decode is reported here, truthfully).

active.description: Whether the decoder is currently in use by a session.

backend.description: OS backend name for hardware decoders.

hardware.description: Whether this is a hardware decoder.

Duration.description:
A duration that may not be known (or may be unbounded, for streams) —
never a sentinel number (§2.2, V3).

oneOf.description: Not (yet) known — may later become known (`timing.duration-known`).

EngineInfo.description:
The engine's self-description (§2.12 `system.get-engine-info`).
`[VERIFY]` — `plugins` is rendered as the id list of registered
plugins; `system.list-plugins` carries the full records.

features.description: Feature-exposure flags enabled for this product (§6.4).

host.description: Host the engine is embedded in (tauri/web/cli/control-server/test).

ErrorCode.description:
The typed failure class (doc 05 §2.13). Every command can fail with
any of these; the catalog (card 1.D4) lists only additions. Wire
form: the kebab-case names of [`ErrorCode::as_str`].

oneOf.description: Unknown field, unknown enum variant, unknown command id (V1).
Scalar range violated (V2) — `details` carries the allowed range.
Operation requires a state the engine is not in.
Superseded by a newer generation (§4.2) — rare on the wire.
Exists in engine, off in product.toml feature exposure.
Host cannot do it (web: no discs, no RTSP, no local FS).
Control server: sensitive op without authorization.

Engine-internal invariant breach — always a bug report, never
user-actionable.

Event.description:
One engine → host event (doc 05 §1.6/§3.1). Generic over the event
payload `E` until the catalog lands. `seq` is engine-global and
strictly increasing; `generation` is present only for pipeline-scoped
events (the staleness rule applies exactly to those); `origin` names
the request that caused the event when attributable.

oneOf.description:
`session.state-changed` — every playback-state transition,
including self-transitions as idempotent confirmations (C8).
Never coalesced.

`session.opening-progress` — network opens, best-effort, ≤ 1 Hz;
absent for local files.

`session.buffering` — enter/while/exit buffering, ≤ 5 Hz; opens
with 0.0 and closes with 1.0.

`timing.time-tick` — continuous position while playing; the only
continuous stream, never queued (§3.4).

`timing.duration-known` — the duration transitioned from
unknown/early-estimate to final; once per change.

`timing.seek-completed` — terminal for the NEWEST seek generation
only (§4.2: superseded seeks are silent). The envelope's `gen`
is the generation that completed; it must match the `Accepted`
response's gen (§1.4 C3).

`timing.seek-failed` — terminal failure for the newest seek
generation; exactly one terminal seek event per completed gen
(§4.3 invariant 4). The envelope's `gen` is the failed
generation.

`tracks.list-ready` — the list became available/relevant: before
first `playing`, after `subtitle.add-file`, after rare changes.
Coalesced ≤ 1 Hz. Delivered before the first `state-changed →
playing` of a session (§4.3 terminal invariant 4).

`tracks.changed` — a selection applied (command) or lost (the
track disappeared, engine-initiated).

`playback.end-of-track` — one elementary stream ended while the
media continues (e.g. audio before video).

`playback.end-of-media` — the media finished; followed by
`state-changed → ended`, then the advance lifecycle (or nothing).

`playback.error` — any stage failure. Fatal errors transition
state to `error` and are always ordered BEFORE their
`state-changed → error` (§3.3). Non-fatal same-code errors are
coalesced per 1 s window with a count `[PROPOSAL]`.

fatal.description: Fatal errors transition the state to `error`.

oneOf.description:
`playback.rate-changed` — `set-rate` echo and future engine-side
rate changes. Not pipeline-scoped.

`audio.device-lost` — the OS removed the active device; migration
or a non-fatal error follows. Not pipeline-scoped.

`audio.device-changed` — the active output device changed
(command or auto-migration). Not pipeline-scoped.

`video.screenshot-saved` — the screenshot was written; completion
evidence for `video.take-screenshot`. Not pipeline-scoped.

`video.backend-changed` — the active render backend changed:
the initial auto-negotiation report, a fallback after a backend
failure (hardware → software present, card 7.C1), or a
user-forced selection. Not pipeline-scoped.

backend.description:
The now-active backend id (redacted vocabulary, e.g.
`"software"`; never a driver path).

reason.description:
Why it changed — the negotiation outcome, the fallback
cause, or `"user"` (display-safe, V8).

oneOf.description:
`playlist.changed` — any playlist model mutation, command- or
engine-initiated; model edits coalesced per 100 ms
`[PROPOSAL]`. Not pipeline-scoped.

`config.setting-changed` — a setting changed through any layer
(user, CLI flag, admin, plugin). Not pipeline-scoped.

`plugins.loaded` — a plugin registered (startup or install flow).
Not pipeline-scoped.

`[VERIFY]` — §3.2 sketches the payload as `{ id, kind, version }`,
but `kind` is the event envelope's discriminator (§5.1): a payload
field of that name is impossible on the wire. The payload field
serializes as `pluginKind`.

pluginKind.description:
Plugin kind (manifest-declared, `[VERIFY]` — string until
the doc 06 taxonomy freezes).

oneOf.description:
`plugins.failed` — a plugin failed to load; the engine continues
without it. Not pipeline-scoped.

`plugins.crashed` — a sandboxed WASM extension crashed; playback
survives (MP §6 error isolation). Not pipeline-scoped.

actionTaken.description: What the engine did about it.

oneOf.description:
`system.log` — a log line for the in-app panel; level-filtered
by `system.set-log-level`. Rate-limited per target (default
100/s then an aggregate "N suppressed") `[PROPOSAL]`.

`media.info-ready` — the metadata snapshot just before first
`playing` (hydration convenience); once per open.

`devices.volume-added` — a local volume or removable medium
appeared (card 7.D1; the discovery crate's watcher emits it
from real mount-table diffs, never fabricated). Not
pipeline-scoped.

id.description: Stable volume id (opaque string; stable while mounted).

volumeKind.description:
The volume's kind (named `volumeKind` on the wire — the
payload's own `kind` slot is taken by the event tag, the
`plugins.loaded` precedent).

oneOf.description:
`devices.volume-removed` — a local volume went away. Not
pipeline-scoped.

Generation.description:
Per-session pipeline generation (doc 05 §4.2): bumped atomically at
accept time of generation-bumping commands and engine-initiated
invalidations. `Generation` ↔ the engine's pipeline generation.

MediaInfo.description:
A media's metadata snapshot (§2.10 `media.get-info`). All strings
are untrusted (V7). Not `Eq`/`Hash` (contains [`TrackInfo`]).

isLive.description: Whether this is a live source.

metadata.description: Free-form container metadata (V7 — render as text, never markup).

source.description: The source the session was opened from.

tracks.description: The track list (same data as the latest `tracks.list-ready`).

OpenOptions.description:
Options for `session.open` (§2.3): schema-validated; an unknown
option is `invalid-argument`. `[VERIFY]` — the "track selectors"
bullet of §2.3 is rendered as one optional selector per track kind.
Not `Eq`/`Hash`: `rate` is an `f32` wire scalar (§2.2 — same class as
[`SeekTarget`] and [`VideoTrackInfo`]).

startTime.description: Start at this position (µs) instead of 0.

PlaybackState.description: The playback state machine (§3.3). Wire: the lowercase names.

oneOf.description: Terminal failure (always accompanied by a fatal `playback.error`).

PlaylistChange.description:
The payload of `playlist.changed` (§3.2): which model mutation
happened, command- or engine-initiated.

source.description: What to enqueue (not opened at enqueue time).

PlaylistItemId.description: Playlist item handle, stable within the playlist lifetime (§2.2).

PlaylistSaveFormat.description:
Playlist serialization format (§2.9 `playlist.save`). Defaults from
the file extension when omitted.

PlaylistSummary.description:
Playlist summary for the snapshot (§2.12). `[VERIFY]` — "playlist
summary + current" rendered as count + current + mode flags.

current.description: Current item, if one is active.

itemCount.description: Number of items in the list.

PluginAction.description:
What the engine did after a sandboxed plugin crashed (§3.2
`plugins.crashed`, MP §6 error isolation).

oneOf.description: The plugin was isolated (kept registered, not run again).

PluginInfo.description:
One registered plugin (§2.12 `system.list-plugins`, MP §6).
`[VERIFY]` — `kind` stays a string until the plugin taxonomy in
doc 06 is frozen into an enum.

PluginSource.description: Where a plugin was loaded from (§2.12 `system.list-plugins`).

oneOf.description: Advance once, then stop at the list end.

RequestId.description:
Monotonic per host connection (doc 05 §4.1): assigned by the sender,
starting at 1, strictly increasing; reuse is forbidden. The engine
echoes it and never interprets it (the control server's anti-replay
check is that host's business).

ResultWire.description: The on-the-wire union of the two response shapes.

SeekKind.description: What kind of seek produced a `timing.seek-completed` (§3.2).

SeekTarget.description:
Where to jump to (§2.2). Wire example (§5.1):
`{ "kind": "relative", "deltaMs": -10000 }`. Not `Eq`/`Hash`:
`Percent`'s fraction is an `f32` wire scalar.

oneOf.description:
µs from media start; clamped to `[0, duration]` when the duration
is known (clamping is truth, not failure — §2.4).

SessionId.description:
Engine-assigned session handle (doc 05 §4.2): `SessionId` ↔ the
engine's session epoch (doc 03 §5).

SessionSummary.description: One live session of the engine (§2.12 `system.get-engine-info`).

SettingValue.description:
A setting value (§2.11 `config.get-setting`/`set-setting`).
`[VERIFY]` — the settings-schema crate owns the authoritative value
model; this wire shape must be reconciled when the two meet in a
host (the shapes coincide for v1 scalar/list values).

SourceSpec.description:
Clean-room source description (§2.2 — no libvlc types). Scheme
support is feature-gated (§6.4); `Disc`/`Capture` are future,
feature-gated variants, not in v1 availability.

oneOf.description: A network URL; scheme support is feature-gated (§6.4).

url.description: The URL, userinfo-free on the wire (V8).

Stage.description:
Where a command failed (doc 05 §2.13 — the command-layer view of the
pipeline; distinct from media-types' `PipelineStage`, which tags
engine-internal errors). Wire form: the kebab-case names of
[`Stage::as_str`] (card 1.D4 serde derives; the 1.D3 test below pins
both spellings to the same strings).

StateSnapshot.description:
Full UI hydration (§2.12 `system.get-state-snapshot`, `[PROPOSAL]`
per doc 05): everything a reconnecting host needs before it
subscribes (§4.4). Called at startup and on reconnect. Not
`Eq`/`Hash` (contains `f32` wire scalars).

time.description: Current position, when a pipeline exists.

oneOf.description: Step to the previous frame (may be a micro-seek, `[03]`).

SubtitleSettings.description:
Subtitle settings block of the snapshot (§2.12). `[VERIFY]` — the
"subtitle settings" bullet rendered as the §2.8 state. Not
`Eq`/`Hash` (`scale` is an `f32`).

TimeRange.description:
A half-open time interval (µs), e.g. one buffered range (§2.10
`media.get-current-time`).

Timestamp.description:
Microseconds since media start; can be negative only in
[`SeekTarget::Relative`] (§2.2). A bare integer on the wire.

TrackChangeKind.description:
The `tracks.changed` track kind (§3.2): [`TrackKind`] plus the
synthetic `secondary-audio` selection.

TrackId.description:
Engine track handle, stable within one session and never reused
inside it (§2.2).

TrackInfo.description:
One track of the current media (§2.2). All strings are untrusted
container metadata (V7). Not `Eq`/`Hash` (contains [`VideoTrackInfo`]).

isDefault.description: Whether the track is the container's default.

isSelected.description: Whether the track is currently selected.

name.description: Name from container metadata (untrusted text, V7).

oneOf.description: Chapters, timed metadata and other non-AV streams.
An external subtitle file added after open.

TrackSelections.description:
Track-selection state for the snapshot (§2.12
`system.get-state-snapshot`). `[VERIFY]` — field set per §2.12's
"tracks + selections" bullet.

TrackSelector.description:
Track selection (§2.2): a specific track, no track, or (meaningful
for subtitles only) the track-selection rules from `product.toml`.

oneOf.description: Select the track with this id.
Apply the product's track-selection rules (subtitles only).

VideoTrackInfo.description:
Video-specific track facts (§2.2 `TrackInfo.video`). Not `Eq`/`Hash`:
`frame_rate` is an `f32` (§2.2's wire scalars are floats by
contract; [`SeekTarget`] likewise).

hdr.description: Whether the stream carries HDR metadata.

VolumeKind.description: The kind of a discovered local volume (7.D1 `devices.volume-added`).

oneOf.description: A filesystem on an internal fixed disk.
A removable medium (USB stick, SD card, …).
